links.comparator_used: Supervised domain adaptation with maximum mean discrepancy (DA MMD) compared with fusion training on merged datasets
links.outcome: AUROC and normalized AUPRC for sepsis prediction in medium-sized target datasets
links.effect: DA MMD: AUROC = 0.720 and nAUPRC = 2.352; fusion training: AUROC = 0.712 and nAUPRC = 2.215; p = 0.02, adjusted p = 0.07
links.quote: For example, DA with maximum mean discrepancy (DA MMD) achieves superior performance in both area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC = 0.720) and normalized area under the precision-recall curve (nAUPRC = 2.352) compared to fusion training (AUROC = 0.712, nAUPRC = 2.215; p = 0.02, adjusted p = 0.07).

links.comparator_used: Retraining, fusion training and supervised domain adaptation (fine-tuning was the adaptation strategy tested)
links.outcome: Sepsis prediction performance of fine-tuning a source model on target-site data
links.effect: Fine-tuning consistently underperformed across all target data sizes (adjusted p < 0.05 vs. DA, fusion, and retraining).
links.quote: Key results demonstrate that fine-tuning consistently underperforms across all data sizes (adjusted p < 0.05 vs. DA, fusion, and retraining) even though it has been the go to method in many prior studies that explored this direction.

design_hint: local adaptation strategy before deployment (retraining, fusion, domain adaptation vs fine-tuning)
